As the company scales production, the resulting stable supply of at-cost oil in our Hemisphere will go toward filling the U.S. strategic petroleum reserve and fulfilling the supply needs of our Great U.S. Military,” the official said.
Rubio called the deal a “huge win for both the American and Venezuelan people.”
“For the Venezuelan people, this deal will bring nearly $100 billion in private investment, support thousands of high-paying jobs, and drive the reconstruction of Venezuela’s economy,” Rubio said shortly after Trump’s announcement.
At the start of the year, the United States captured Venezuela’s Nicolás Maduro in a large-scale military operation, bringing the leader and his wife to New York to face criminal charges. After the military operation, Trump said American companies would work to rebuild Venezuela’s oil industry.
In January, Venezuelan lawmakers approved a law change, backed by Rodríguez, to make it easier for foreign companies to take part in the country’s oil industry.
Venezuela has more proven oil reserves than any nation on the planet.
This story has been updated with additional details.
CNN’s Mauricio Torres contributed to this report.

sources.news_title: U.S. has entered deal with Venezuela to take control of 65 billion barrels of oil reserves, says Trump
sources.text:
President Donald Trump on Friday (August 28, 2026) said the U.S. has entered an agreement with Venezuela to take control of 65 billion barrels of the South American country’s oil reserves.
Mr. Trump in a social media post announced the agreement he said was negotiated by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodriguez.
“The United States of America has just entered into an Agreement with the Country of Venezuela on, THE BIGGEST OIL DEAL IN WORLD HISTORY!” Mr. Trump wrote.
The Venezuelan government’s press office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The announcement of the deal comes nearly nine months after the U.S. military at Trump’s direction carried out an operation to capture Venezuela’s President Nicolás Maduro and spirit him to the United States to face federal narcoterrorism and drug trafficking charges.
Mr. Trump faces mounting pressure to address high gas prices as the war in Iran on Friday (August 28, 2026) reached a six-month milestone with no conclusion in sight. The U.S. has tapped its strategic petroleum reserves, which in early August fell below 300 million barrels, down by more than 100 million barrels since the start of 2026.
The U.S.-Israel war against Iran has led to a dramatic slowdown of Gulf oil moving through the Strait of Hormuz, which about 20 per cent of the world petroleum passed through prior to the conflict.
The average price of gas in the U.S. stood at about $4.09 a gallon on Friday (August 28, 2026), according to AAA. The average price was $3.21 at the same time last year.
Mr. Trump in his social media post Friday (August 28, 2026) evening alluded to the Venezuela deal being part of a private partnership. The White House did not immediately reply to a request for comment about the private sector partners involved in the deal, and details on how the arrangement would work were not provided.
Persuading big American oil companies to return the region could face headwinds given and decades of badly damaged infrastructure.
Days after the ouster of Mr. Maduro, Mr. Trump gathered oil executives at the White House and called on them to rush back into Venezuela. Executives expressed interest in the opportunity but there was also a measure of caution given their past experience in the country.
Darren Woods, CEO of ExxonMobil, the largest U.S. oil company, said at that moment he saw the country as “un-investable.” But Trump has insisted that his administration has brought a measure of stability to Venezuela.
He has argued that Venezuela stole U.S. oil when former Venezuelan President Hugo Chavez’s moved decades ago to nationalise hundreds of foreign-owned assets, including those owned by American oil companies.
Ms. Rodriguez, in one of her early moves after taking power, signed a law that opens the nation’s oil sector to privatization and reversed a bedrock tenet of the self-proclaimed socialist movement that had ruled the country for more than two decades.
Mr. Rubio said on X that the agreement would usher in $100 billion in private investment into Venezuela and lead to lower gas prices in the United States.
“This deal is a huge win for both the American and Venezuelan people,” Mr. Rubio posted.
Venezuela has one of the largest oil reserves in the world, with an estimated 303 billion barrels of crude oil in the ground. That’s about 17% of the world’s supply, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.
Unlike other parts of the world, where geologists have to search for untapped oil, the reserves under Venezuela’s soil are largely mapped and known, experts say. But because of dilapidated infrastructure, the country only produces about 1% of the world’s oil.

Trump calls agreement the ‘biggest oil deal in world history’

WHAT WARSH'S JACKSON HOLE SPEECH SIGNALS ABOUT WHERE INTEREST RATES ARE HEADED

The Latest: Trump says US will take control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuela’s oil reserves
sources.text:
President Donald Trump on Friday said the U.S. has entered an agreement with Venezuela to take control of 65 billion barrels of the South American country’s oil reserves. Trump in a social media post announced the agreement he said was negotiated by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodriguez.
The administration also has appealed the latest ruling blocking his mail voting order from taking effect, the latest twist in a court fight unfolding days before the first states begin sending out mail ballots.
The notice of appeal filed Friday comes after a federal judge in Boston handed down a new decision blocking implementation of an executive order from Trump for the next two weeks. The Supreme Court previously allowed the plan to move ahead on procedural grounds, but hasn’t decided whether it’s legal.
Also, Trump has reached an awkward moment in his second term as the U.S.-Israel war against Iran began six months ago Friday. It’s a notable milestone for a Republican leader who repeatedly assured Americans that attacking Iran would be a “little excursion” over in weeks.

There is ‘strong support’ at UN to extend peacekeeping force in southern Lebanon for limited period, 2 UN diplomats said
The Security Council met behind closed doors Friday and discussed a request by Lebanon’s government to extend the mandate for the 8,100-member force, which is supposed to end on Dec. 31, the two diplomats with knowledge of the discussion said.
While there was “strong support” among the 15 council members to extend the mandate for the force, known as UNIFIL, it wasn’t unanimous, the diplomats said, speaking on condition of anonymity because the meeting was closed.
Israel has pressed for the closure of UNIFIL for years, and last year the United States, its closest ally, succeeded in forcing its closure on Dec. 31. But that was before the latest Israel-Hezbollah war, which erupted on March 2. Despite a June 20 truce, airstrikes and clashes have continued.
The two diplomats said U.S. Ambassador Mike Waltz attended Friday’s council meeting, listened to the members, and didn’t say yes or no to a limited extension of UNIFIL.
— By Edith M. Lederer
Vance, Zeldin call for probe into Biden administration’s response to Ohio train derailment
Vance joined U.S. EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin on Friday in calling for an independent investigation into the Biden administration’s handling of the disastrous 2023 train derailment East Palestine, Ohio.
Vance and Zeldin made their request to the EPA Office of Inspector General as midterm elections are under way. To explain the timing 3.5 years after the fiery crash, they cited “troubling media reports” and new documents that have recently come to light.
“No stone should be left unturned,” they said.
The EPA oversaw Norfolk Southern railroad’s cleanup after the derailment, but residents questioned whether the agency did enough to ensure they were safe and shared everything known about the risks of being exposed to chemicals that were released and burned.
Vance was a U.S. senator representing Ohio at the time of the crash, as was Democrat Sherrod Brown, who’s running this year after losing a reelection bid in 2024.
FBI no longer treating an applicant’s experience with prostitution as automatic bar against hiring
The FBI is no longer treating an applicant’s prior encounters with prostitutes as an automatic bar against employment.
The change comes amid broader concerns about a loosening of recruitment requirements at the nation’s premier federal law enforcement agency.
The bureau still intends to dismiss applicants who are revealed during the vetting process to have engaged in prostitution within the last 10 years, three or more times overall or while in a position of trust.
That’s according to guidance issued this past spring and described by a person familiar with the matter who was not authorized to discuss internal decision-making and spoke on condition of anonymity.
For others, it will allow for consideration of the context of the conduct rather than treat it as grounds for an automatic rejection from the FBI’s hiring process.
— By Eric Tucker
National Park Service backs Trump’s arch, despite its impact on Washington’s sightline
Its report released Friday says the 250-foot-tall (76-meter) memorial arch is likely to disrupt the historical significance of dozens of sites near its planned location adjacent to Memorial Bridge.
Many of Washington’s monuments, buildings and sites have been carefully planned over decades to reflect significant moments in the nation’s history and evoke symbolism in being connected by sightline to other sites. arch will disturb the sightline between more iconic Washington landmarks than anticipated, report says
But the Park Service report says “the same characteristics that make Memorial Circle sensitive from a preservation perspective are also the characteristics that make it the historically appropriate location for the undertaking.”
Far-right British provocateur Milo Yiannopoulos arrested by US immigration enforcement
Immigration officials said that Yiannopoulos was arrested at Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport
They accused him of entering the United States legally in May 2019 through New York City. An immigration judge issued a final order of removal on July 22 after Yiannopoulos failed to show up for his immigration hearing, a DHS spokesperson wrote in an email.
“He chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation’s laws,” a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security wrote in an emailed statement.
ICE’s online detainee locator doesn’t say where Yiannopoulos is being held but directs family and legal representatives to the agency’s office in Alexandria, Louisiana, a deportation hub for international flights.
Sen. Bernie Sanders ties progressive platform to Martin Luther King Jr.’s civil rights message
“As you all well know, the message he delivered back in 1963 is as true today as it was back then,” Sanders told a crowd of demonstrators from the steps of the Lincoln Memorial.
Sanders addressed the crowd on the 63rd anniversary of King’s iconic 1963 March on Washington. Sanders noted the official mission of the march was “for jobs and freedom,” noting the economic dimension of King’s message.
Sanders also made an appeal to Black voters for his progressive vision.
“While this economic crisis impacts all of our people, all races, creeds, and people in every corner of our country, it continues to disproportionately affect the Black community,” said Sanders.
International Space Station gets a call from Trump
Trump joined a call to American astronauts on the International Space Station during a Friday visit to NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.
Officials said it was the first time a sitting president called the station from Mission Control.
Trump congratulated the crew and said he admired their bravery.
“I wouldn’t do it. I will tell you right now, I hate to admit it,” Trump said. “But some people love it more than anything. And you have amazing courage.”
Crew members talked about their time on the station, saying they’re preparing for an upcoming spacewalk. They said they were excited to hear about Trump’s newly announced U.S. Space Academy.
When they get back to Earth, they will be invited to the White House, Trump said: “We’ll see you in the Oval Office, OK?”
Trump administration to appeal mail ballot decision
The White House plans to appeal a judge’s order blocking changes to mail voting ahead of the midterms.
Spokeswoman Lauren Bis said in statement Friday that the Trump administration will immediately appeal the order handed down late Thursday by a Boston-based judge.
Under Trump’s executive order, the U.S. Postal Service could refuse to deliver ballots from states that do not submit lists of eligible voters and follow a uniform envelope style.
With the first mail ballots set to go out next week, U.S. District Court Judge Indira Talwani found that states don’t have the time or money to produce new mail ballots and upload voter data.
Bis called the plan a series of commonsense measures that would protect ballot security.
A lawsuit from Democrat-controlled states says the new rules would cause chaos and leave out eligible voters.
Jeffries says Dems still could win majority in House despite GOP-led redistricting
In an interview with AP during Friday’s march for civil rights on the National Mall, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Democrats could still win a majority in the U.S. House despite GOP-led redistricting efforts in Southern states.
“We’re going to win all across the country, up and down the ballot,” Jeffries said. “We only have to flip about five or six seats, and that’s really what we’re going to do.”
Egypt acknowledges US ban on government-owned bank’s UAE branches
Egypt’s foreign ministry and central bank are communicating with U.S. officials with regard to a recent decision by the U.S. Treasury to limit the operations of Banque Misr in the United Arab Emirates, according to a statement issued by the Central Bank of Egypt on Friday.
“The CBE affirms that this measure is limited to the bank’s branches in the UAE and only to its dollar transfers,” read the statement adding that the ban does not affect any other Egyptian bank and does not even extend to the Banque Misr’s operations inside Egypt or to any of its overseas branches.
“The Central Bank of Egypt affirms the strength and resilience of all banks operating in Egypt,” said the statement.
The Trump administration announced that it is taking steps to sever the Emirati branches of Banque Misr, Egypt’s second-largest bank, from access to the U.S. financial system on grounds that the financial institution was serving as an economic lifeline to Tehran’s leadership.
California sues Trump administration for ending state’s offshore wind project
State officials announced the lawsuit Friday over the administration buying back the lease for Golden State Wind. They say the cancellation will harm the state’s clean energy and climate goals, and economy.
The Trump administration is buying back offshore wind leases from energy companies as it seeks to discourage the expansion of wind energy in favor of fossil fuels.
Golden State Wind can recover about $120 million in lease fees after the same amount is invested in oil and gas development.
Interior Secretary Doug Burgum says companies are shifting investment back toward dependable, secure energy infrastructure.
Trump loses again in bid to erase his hush money conviction
A federal judge rejected the president’s bid to move the state court case to federal court and have it dismissed on presidential immunity grounds.
Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein reiterated his earlier finding against Trump, saying that the reasons Trump cited for renewing his request were “neither new nor legally sufficient.”
The judge added: “He has failed to show good cause and diligence.”
It is the third time Hellerstein has blocked Trump from having the U.S. District Court in Manhattan seize control of the case from the New York court where he was tried and convicted.
Trump announces new Space Academy to join military academies
Speaking at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston on Friday, Trump said he is creating a U.S. Space Academy to train future generations for ambitious space missions.
Looking ahead to future missions to Mars and beyond, Trump said the nation needs to train “an entire generation of skilled service members, engineers and civil operators.”
Trump said he would soon decide a location for the academy, which he said will match the rigor of West Point, the Air Force Academy and other military academies.
“I said I’ll do it, but it’s got to be top line, it’s got to be the equivalent of the others,” he said.
Trump signed an executive order on Friday creating the new academy.
Trump sends good luck to team involved in weekend Roman Space Telescope launch
Trump is sending his best wishes to a team that on Sunday will launch the Roman Space Telescope, which NASA says will help settle questions in the areas of dark energy, exoplanets and astrophysics.
In his remarks at the ceremony, Trump noted the telescope will “help unlock the secrets of the universe.”
“To everyone involved here at NASA, good luck this weekend,” he added. “It’s a big deal.”
The telescope is named after Nancy Grace Roman, the first woman to hold an executive position at NASA and who helped with development of the Hubble Space Telescope.
Vance will speak at Republican Jewish leaders gathering – but his speech isn’t set to be public
Leading GOP voices are planning to address the Republican Jewish Coalition annual conference – but Vance’s remarks are listed as closed to reporters.
Vance, Indiana Sen. Jim Banks and Yechiel Leiter, Israel’s ambassador to the United States, are all speaking at the gathering being held Sunday and Monday in Las Vegas, but are doing so behind closed doors only.
The public speech program is packed with other major GOP leaders, however. That includes members of Trump’s Cabinet, senators, House lawmakers and candidates vying for key Senate seats in North Carolina, Georgia and Michigan during November’s midterm elections.
Vance is widely seen as a 2028 presidential hopeful, and addressing the influential gathering is common for those likely to run for president. Also on the public speaking list is Vivek Ramaswamy, a 2024 presidential candidate now running for Ohio governor.
Top Democrat on Armed Services committee calls Iran war a ‘policy failure’
Sen. Jack Reed of Rhode Island said Trump promised he would destroy Iran’s nuclear program, eliminate its missile and drone arsenal, and topple the regime in a matter of weeks.
“Six months later, not a single objective has been achieved,” Reed said. “Indeed, he has weakened our position in the Middle East and the world significantly.”
He called it a policy failure of “historic consequence” and said it was past time for accountability.
Jeffries says he doesn’t regret meeting with Jared Kushner
In an interview with The Associated Press, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said he did not regret meeting with Trump’s son-in-law.
Jeffries said he still expected Democrats to retake control of the U.S. House despite the party’s internal debates between its progressive and moderate wings, as well as Republican-led congressional redistricting efforts across the country.
“We’re going to win all across the country, up and down the ballot. We only have to flip about five or six seats, and that’s really what we’re going to do. It is a call to action,” said Jeffries.
Martin Luther King Jr.’s son says the state of the country would disappoint his father
Martin Luther King III told the AP during Friday’s voting right rally at the National Mall that the work of the Civil Rights movement “is further eroding” in the wake of the Supreme Courts’ April ruling that reinterpreted key provisions of the Voting Rights Act of 1965.
King III also said that his father, who worked so hard for that law, would be disappointed with the state of the country.
“Had he lived, we’d be on a totally different trajectory,” King said. “These would not be issues; they would have been resolved.”
US revokes visa of former Iraqi finance minister who won 2022 ‘International Women of Courage’ award
The Trump administration has revoked the U.S. visa of a former Iraqi finance minister who was honored in 2022 with an “International Women of Courage” award by the State Department.
The department said Friday it had revoked the visa of Taif Sami Mohammed Al Shakarchi, who served as Iraq’s finance minister from 2022 until July. Earlier this month she was implicated by Iraqi authorities in a possible corruption scheme.
The department said her visa was revoked after the FBI added her to its “terrorism watchlist.” It was not clear why she had been added to the watchlist but officials said she had left the United States before her visa revoked.
US Treasury targets Egyptian Bank’s UAE branches under ‘Operation Economic Outcast’
The Trump administration is taking steps to limit an Egyptian bank’s operations in the United Arab Emirates, accusing the financial institution of serving as an economic lifeline to Tehran’s leadership as the U.S. war in Iran reaches the six-month mark.
Under a new rule proposed by the U.S. Treasury, the Emirati branches of Banque Misr, Egypt’s second-largest bank, would be severed from access to the U.S. financial system.
This comes after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent held a presser earlier in the week announced “Operation Economic Outcast,” warning countries that do business with Iran to sever their financial ties or face retaliation from the U.S.
US goals have shifted after 6 months of Iran war. The Strait of Hormuz is now a top concern
When Trump launched the war with Iran in late February, he forecast it would last four weeks to five weeks. Six months later, there still is no off-ramp in sight, despite Trump’s repeated assertions that the war has been won or a deal to resolve it was nearly complete.
A June memorandum of understanding designed to pave the way to end the war has fallen by the wayside. U.S. stockpiles of key weapons have diminished, and the Republican administration has pivoted to pressuring Iran economically rather than conducting more strikes.
The administration described various goals for the war:
1. Stop Iran from having a nuclear weapon
2. Reopen the Strait of Hormuz
3. Destroy Iran’s ability to fire missiles
4. Destroy Iran’s defense industrial base
5. Eliminate Iran’s navy and air force
6. Protect America’s Middle Eastern allies
7. Cut off support for Iranian proxy groups
▶ Read more about these objectives and where they stand
Sharpton says this year’s march is the most important yet
“We’ve been doing these marches for years, but this is probably the most important because this is the first year we are marching that the voting rights bill has been nullified by the Supreme Court,” Sharpton, founder of the National Action Network, said in an interview with The Associated Press.
The march opened with prayer and statements from Interfaith Alliance representatives who spoke on diversity, equity and inclusion practices, voting rights and systemic racism.
Thousands converge on National Mall in Washington to support voting rights
Friday’s march follows changes to voting laws and redistricting that civil rights groups have condemned as detrimental to racial justice and Black Americans in particular.
The 2026 “Defend the Vote” March on Washington, is organized by the Rev. Al Sharpton and Martin Luther King III and echoes the Rev. Martin Luther King Jr.’s 1963 march.
The U.S. Supreme Court’s landmark April decision in Louisiana v. Callais reinterpreted the Voting Rights Act, allowing Southern states to redraw congressional maps in ways that erode equal representation in Black communities.

sources.news_title: Trump says new Venezuelan oil deal will "substantially lower" gas prices
sources.text:
President Donald Trump announced what he called the "biggest oil deal in world history," saying the United States has secured majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of proven oil reserves in Venezuela through an agreement involving the Venezuelan government and private-sector partners.
In a Truth Social post Friday, Trump said the arrangement would come at "no cost to the American taxpayer," more than double U.S. oil reserves and help lower gasoline prices.
Trump said Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth helped negotiate the deal alongside Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodríguez, describing it as a historic step in strengthening ties between the two countries.
Rubio posted on X, "This deal is a huge win for both the American and Venezuelan people. It demonstrates how President Trump's bold foreign policy is driving America First wins: securing stable reserves and low-cost oil in our Hemisphere and lowering gas prices here at home. For the Venezuelan people, this deal will bring nearly $100 billion in private investment, support thousands of high-paying jobs, and drive the reconstruction of Venezuela's economy."
A U.S. official told Newsweek on Friday night that the deal would give the U.S. an effective 55 percent output of a new Venezuelan oil venture through equity and oil purchased at cost. Rodríguez has granted a private company—a joint effort between the U.S. government and a private operator in Venezuela—100-year concessions to fields holding 63 billion barrels of proven reserves, potentially making it the world's second-largest corporate holder after Saudi Aramco, the official said.
Trump posted in full, "BREAKING NEWS: The United States of America has just entered into an Agreement with the Country of Venezuela on, THE BIGGEST OIL DEAL IN WORLD HISTORY! At my direction, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, working closely with Highly Respected Interim President of Venezuela, Delcy Rodriguez, and, through a partnership with private business, have secured majority U.S. control of more than 65 BILLION BARRELS of proven Oil Reserves in Venezuela, at no cost to the American Taxpayer. This Historic Transaction MORE THAN DOUBLES American Oil Reserves, greatly increases our Oil Supply, and will substantially lower Gas Prices for all Americans, long into the future, while helping to continue to set Venezuela on a course toward Tremendous Success and Great Prosperity. This Transaction will greatly strengthen the already growing relationship between Venezuela and the United States! Thank you for your attention to this groundbreaking matter. MAKE AMERICA GREAT AGAIN! President DONALD J. TRUMP."
Which States Have the Highest Gas Prices?
The national average price for a gallon of gas is $4.09 as of Friday, according to AAA.
For the first time, the national average has remained above $4 per gallon every day in August. The month is now on track to become the most expensive August on record at the pump, AAA reported, surpassing the previous record set in 2022.
The organization said the national average is 1 cent lower than last week, but that there’s been “little movement” on the crude oil front.
“Due to continued volatility in the Strait of Hormuz, crude oil prices remain in the $80 per barrel range,” AAA said in a Thursday update.

5 States With the Lowest Gas Prices

- Texas: $3.63
- Mississippi: $3.65
- South Carolina: $3.67
- Louisiana: $3.69
U.S.-Venezuelan Relations
Trump’s announcement comes against the backdrop of a major transformation in relations between Washington and Caracas.
Nearly nine months ago, U.S. forces, at Trump’s direction, captured Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and brought him to the United States to face federal narcoterrorism and drug trafficking charges.
The Trump administration has since expanded U.S. involvement in Venezuela’s energy sector, which contains the world’s largest proven crude oil reserves.
Venezuela holds some of the world’s largest oil reserves, with an estimated 303 billion barrels of crude—about 17 percent of the global total, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. Much of the country’s oil is already mapped and known, unlike in other regions where geologists are still searching for untapped reserves.
Newsweek reached out to the Venezuelan government for comment.

West Texas Intermediate crude prices fell 4% this week, marking the first losing week of the last three. Still, prices have jumped more than 24% since the U.S. war with Iran began.
Trump's war with Iran has hampered transit in the Strait of Hormuz, a globally important passageway for crude. Only a handful of ships have recently crossed through Hormuz each day, down from levels of around 100 seen a year ago, according to the International Monetary Fund's PortWatch tracker.

sources.news_title: Trump Says US Secured Control of Some Venezuelan Oil Reserves
US enters into oil agreement with Venezuela, Donald Trump says
sources.text:
President Donald Trump on Friday announced an unprecedented US push to take control of a fifth of Venezuela's vast oil reserves, betting that American companies can revive the OPEC nation's battered energy industry while delivering a new source of crude to help bring down US fuel prices.
Trump provided few details about the agreement, saying only that the US had secured majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuela's proven oil reserves through a partnership with private business.
"At my direction, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, working closely with Highly Respected Interim President of Venezuela, Delcy Rodriguez, and, through a partnership with private business, have secured majority US control of more than 65 BILLION BARRELS of proven Oil Reserves in Venezuela, at no cost to the American Taxpayer," Trump wrote on Truth Social.
The announcement comes after weeks of US-Venezuelan negotiations over a deal that would give American companies long-term access to a group of Venezuelan oilfields and guarantee the resulting crude supply to the United States.
Sources previously told Reuters that a lease model was under consideration, with fields potentially auctioned to US producers, but the arrangement could face legal and constitutional challenges in Venezuela, where the state retains control over core oil industry activities.
The deal would represent a dramatic expansion of the US role in Venezuela's oil industry as the Trump administration seeks to revive the country's deteriorated production and secure more crude for US refineries. Venezuela holds the world's largest proven oil reserves but produces only about 1.25 million barrels per day, far below its potential after years of underinvestment, mismanagement and sanctions.
Trump's announcement provided few details on the structure of the agreement, the fields or companies involved, or how the United States would exercise majority control over the reserves.
Trump administration under pressure to secure stable oil flow
Since the US captured and removed former President Nicolas Maduro from power in January, Washington has been trying to secure a stable flow of Venezuelan crude for US refineries while promoting American investment in the country's oil industry.
The Trump administration is under pressure ahead of midterm elections scheduled later this year over rising gasoline prices, which could be eased through cheaper oil supplies and expanded output. The US also has been looking for solutions to replenish its Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the oil stockpile, including the possibility of crude swaps with US producers.

sources.text:
President Donald Trump announced Friday that the United States had reached an agreement with Venezuela securing majority U.S. control of more than 65 billion barrels of oil reserves, touting the deal as a major boost to U.S. energy security and a potential long-term answer to rising gas prices.
Trump announced the agreement in a Truth Social post, calling it “THE BIGGEST OIL DEAL IN WORLD HISTORY.”
The president said Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth negotiated the deal with Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodriguez and private businesses.
“This Historic Transaction MORE THAN DOUBLES American Oil Reserves, greatly increases our Oil Supply, and will substantially lower Gas Prices for all Americans, long into the future,” Trump wrote.
Trump said the agreement comes “at no cost to the American Taxpayer” and argued that it will strengthen the increasingly close relationship between Washington and Caracas.
Trump did not identify the private businesses participating in the deal or provide details about the agreement’s structure or how the United States would exercise majority control over the reserves.
The announcement follows the Trump administration’s dramatic intervention in Venezuela earlier this year, when U.S. forces captured then-President Nicolás Maduro and brought him to the United States to face federal narcoterrorism and drug-trafficking charges.
In the months since Maduro’s removal, Trump has repeatedly emphasized Venezuela’s enormous petroleum reserves and the possibility of bringing American energy companies back into the country.
Venezuela possesses the largest proven oil reserves in the world, with roughly 303 billion barrels of crude oil beneath its territory, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. The 65 billion barrels cited by Trump represent a substantial portion of the country’s known reserves.
Venezuela has historically produced only a fraction of the oil its reserves would suggest. Years of economic collapse, sanctions, government mismanagement and deteriorating infrastructure have crippled the country’s oil industry, leaving Venezuela responsible for only about 1% of global oil production despite possessing roughly 17% of the world’s oil reserves.
Developing the reserves covered by the agreement could give the United States a significant new source of oil, but any effect on supply would depend on how quickly production could be expanded.
The timing is particularly significant as Americans face elevated energy prices and the Trump administration attempts to manage the economic fallout from the war with Iran. The conflict has disrupted global oil markets, particularly through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping corridor for crude.
Oil prices have risen sharply since the conflict began, while the United States has drawn down its Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) to levels not seen in decades, per CNBC.
The reserve fell below 300 million barrels earlier this month, more than 100 million barrels below its level at the beginning of 2026.
The average price of gasoline in the United States was roughly $4.09 per gallon on Thursday, according to AAA. Trump has repeatedly argued that increasing American energy production and securing reliable supplies from friendly nations can help bring those prices back down.
“This Transaction will greatly strengthen the already growing relationship between Venezuela and the United States,” Trump wrote.
The agreement could mark a significant new phase in that relationship if American companies invest in Venezuela’s long-neglected oil infrastructure and substantially increase production. Its ultimate effect on American supply and gasoline prices will depend on how quickly the oil can be developed and brought to market.

Trump says U.S. is taking partial control of Venezuela’s vast oil reserves
President Donald Trump on Friday announced an unprecedented U.S. push to take control of a fifth of Venezuela’s vast oil reserves, betting that American companies can revive the OPEC nation’s battered energy industry while delivering a new source of crude to help bring down U.S. fuel prices.
Trump provided few details about the agreement, saying only that the U.S. had secured majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuela’s proven oil reserves through a partnership with private business.
The South American nation’s leader welcomed the agreement, saying it would boost the economy and government revenue.
The new deal would represent a dramatic expansion of the U.S. role in Venezuela’s oil industry as the Trump administration seeks to revive the country’s production and secure more crude for U.S. refineries. Venezuela holds the world’s largest proven oil reserves but produces only about 1.25 million barrels per day, far below its potential after years of underinvestment, mismanagement and sanctions.
RUBIO CALLS DEAL A WIN-WIN
“At my direction, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, working closely with Highly Respected Interim President of Venezuela, Delcy Rodriguez, and, through a partnership with private business, have secured majority U.S. control of more than 65 BILLION BARRELS of proven Oil Reserves in Venezuela, at no cost to the American Taxpayer,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.
The announcement followed weeks of U.S.-Venezuelan negotiations over a deal that would give American companies long-term access to a group of Venezuelan oilfields and guarantee the resulting crude supply to the United States.
Venezuelan officials are preparing to sign agreements next week granting new oil exploration and production rights to a number of companies, particularly U.S. firms.
Sources have told Reuters that a lease model was under consideration, with fields potentially auctioned to U.S. producers, but the arrangement could face legal and constitutional challenges in Venezuela, where the state retains control over core oil industry activities.
Trump did not disclose the structure of the agreement, the fields or companies involved or how the United States would exercise majority control over the reserves. A list seen by Reuters shows the fields are in the Orinoco Belt and Lake Maracaibo regions.
Rubio described the agreement as a win for both countries, saying on X that it would secure stable, low-cost oil for the United States and help lower gasoline prices.
For Venezuela, Rubio said the deal would bring nearly $100 billion in private investment, support thousands of high-paying jobs and help rebuild the country’s economy.
Rodriguez, who became interim leader after the U.S. seized President Nicolas Maduro in January, said late on Friday that the agreement would allow for a significant increase in production through the development of 17 strategic fields and result in tax revenue for the country totaling $209 billion.
“These investments will contribute not only to the recovery and modernization of our industry, but also to our country’s economic growth, the energy security of our hemisphere, and greater balance in international markets,” she said in a statement.
LEGAL BASIS, FINANCIAL STRUCTURE UNCLEAR
Analysts said they needed to see more details on the agreement’s legal and financial structure before assessing whether it could attract significant investment.
Also unclear is whether the deal will lower gasoline prices in the short term, as developing the infrastructure needed to produce, transport and refine Venezuela’s heavy crude could take years.
David Goldwyn, president of Goldwyn Global Strategies, said it was unclear whether a U.S. government lease would have a legal basis under Venezuela’s constitution and its new hydrocarbons law, adding that there is “no precedent for having the U.S. government enter into a lease to operate oil fields.”
Goldwyn also questioned whether the plan would address the obstacles that have deterred investment in Venezuela for years. “It is hard to see how this kind of arrangement would accelerate investment at any material scale,” he said, citing political uncertainty, an inadequate power grid, limited export capacity and government discretion over the industry.
Since removing Maduro, Washington has been trying to secure a stable flow of Venezuelan crude for U.S. refineries while promoting American investment in the country’s oil industry.
The Trump administration is under pressure ahead of midterm elections in November to mollify consumer concerns over rising gasoline prices. Cheaper oil supplies and expanded output could help.
The U.S. also has been looking for solutions to replenish its Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the nation’s oil stockpile, including the possibility of crude swaps with U.S. producers.
Venezuela nationalized its oil industry in the 1970s, putting state-run PDVSA at its center. Under then-President Hugo Chavez, the government tightened control, forcing foreign producers into state-led joint ventures and later expropriating assets, including projects operated by ExxonMobil and ConocoPhillips.
Under Maduro’s rule Venezuela’s production fell sharply.

sources.news_title: Trump says US will take control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuela’s oil reserves
sources.text:
Trump says US will take control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuela’s oil reserves
Loading article...
President Donald Trump on Friday said the United States has entered into an agreement with Venezuela to take control of 65 billion barrels of the South American country’s oil reserves.
Trump, in a social media post, announced the agreement he said was negotiated by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodriguez.
“The United States of America has just entered into an Agreement with the Country of Venezuela on THE BIGGEST OIL DEAL IN WORLD HISTORY!” Trump wrote.
The Venezuelan government’s press office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The announcement of the deal comes nearly nine months after the US military, at Trump’s direction, carried out an operation to capture Venezuela’s president Nicolás Maduro and spirit him to the United States to face federal narcoterrorism and drug trafficking charges.
Trump faces mounting pressure to address high gas prices as the war in Iran reaches a six-month milestone with no conclusion in sight.
The US has tapped its strategic petroleum reserves, which in early August fell below 300 million barrels, down by more than 100 million barrels since the start of 2026.
The US-Israel war against Iran has led to a dramatic slowdown of Gulf oil moving through the Strait of Hormuz, through which about 20% of the world's petroleum passed prior to the conflict.
The average price of gas in the U.S. stood at about $4.09 a gallon on Friday, according to AAA. The average price was $3.21 at the same time last year.
Trump in his social media post Friday evening alluded to the Venezuela deal being part of a private partnership.
The White House did not immediately reply to a request for comment about the private sector partners involved in the deal, and details on how the arrangement would work were not provided.
Persuading big American oil companies to return to the region could face headwinds given the unrest and decades of badly damaged infrastructure.
Days after the ouster of Maduro, Trump gathered oil executives at the White House and called on them to rush back into Venezuela. Executives expressed interest in the opportunity, but there was also a measure of caution given their past experience in the country.
Darren Woods, CEO of ExxonMobil, the largest US oil company, said at that moment he saw the country as “un-investable.”
But Trump has insisted that his administration has brought a measure of stability to Venezuela.
He has argued that Venezuela stole US oil when former Venezuelan President Hugo Chavez’s moved decades ago to nationalize hundreds of foreign-owned assets, including those owned by American oil companies.
Venezuela has one of the largest oil reserves in the world, with an estimated 303 billion barrels of crude oil in the ground.
That’s about 17% of the world’s supply, according to the US Energy Information Administration.
Unlike other parts of the world, where geologists have to search for untapped oil, the reserves under Venezuela’s soil are largely mapped and known, experts say.
But because of dilapidated infrastructure, the country only produces about 1% of the world’s oil.

The Reform UK party, led by Nigel Farage, has introduced an Election Integrity Bill aimed at overhauling Britain’s voting laws to combat electoral fraud and foreign interference.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED: Nigel Farage’s Reform UK has proposed mandatory English proficiency checks to vote, among other election integrity measures.
📺 DETAIL: Reform’s newly unveiled Election Integrity Billwould remove voting rights for Commonwealth citizens, limit postal (mail-in) voting, and implement mandatory English proficiency testsat polling stations. A Commonwealth citizen is someone who is a citizen of a member state of the Commonwealth of Nations, a voluntary association of nations, the vast majority of which were former colonies or dependencies of the British Empire. Under British law, Commonwealth citizens are currently allowed to vote in British elections, even if they do not hold British citizenship.This covers swathes of Africa and Asia and is largely not reciprocal. The measures to limit postal voting are intended to combat mail-in ballot fraud, similar to initiatives pursued in the United States by President Donald J. Trump. The bill also contains provisions against “family voting” and voter coercion. Family voting is a form of electoral fraud in which a family enters a voting booth together, with husbands, in particular, able to control how their wives and children cast their ballots. The measures would also ensure that election material is only published in British languages such as English, Welsh, and Gaelic, or Braille or British Sign Language (BSL) for the visually and audibly impaired.
💬 KEY QUOTE: “With every election, our democracy is being systematically eroded.Britain’s electoral system—once the envy of the world—now buckles under the strain of uncontrolled immigration. In too many parts of the country, elections have been captured by foreign conflicts and sectarian interests, not by what is best for Britain. Reform UK will not stand by while our political system is undermined. Britain should be run in the interests of the British people. That’s why we are introducing these changes to save our democracy,” said Danny Kruger, Reform UK Member of Parliament (MP) and head of the party’s Department for Preparing for Government.
🎯 IMPACT: If enacted, the bill could fundamentally reshape British voting practices,representing a major step forward for election integrity in the country. Britain already requires voter ID to participate in elections, so this bill would build upon past victories. The bill is a response to potential and verified cases of voter fraud at recent elections.
Today I am tabling amendments to the Representation of the People Bill to end Commonwealth voting, restrict postal voting, end foreign language election materials, and crack down on coercive ‘family voting’.

The proposed constitutional amendment would have allowed lawmakers to redraw congressional districts while removing existing requirements that districts remain compact and follow natural boundaries.
📺 DETAIL: Democrats currently hold seven of Maryland’s eight seats in the U.S. House of Representatives, with Republican Representative Andy Harrisas the state’s lone GOP lawmaker on the Eastern Shore. Critics of the proposal argued that eliminating the mapmaking restrictions empowers the Democrats to redraw Harris’s district in a way that makes it more difficult for the Republican to retain. County Circuit Court Judge Robert Thompson ruled Wednesday that the measure missed a state deadline requiring ballot summaries to be certified by July 1. The Maryland Senate Republican Caucus welcomed the decision, arguing that the dispute was about enforcing election laws rather than preventing voters from having a say. The ruling comes amid a broader national battle over congressional redistricting ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, with both parties seeking to maximize their advantage. Similar Democratic redistricting efforts have faced legal setbacks in Virginia, while Republicans have pursued favorable maps in Texas and Democrats have backed a redistricting effort in California.
💬 KEY QUOTE: “The case has never been about preventing Marylanders from having a voice, it’s been about ensuring that before voters are asked to amend the constitution, the state first complies with the constitution and the election procedures established by law.” – Maryland Senate Republican Caucus statement
🎯 IMPACT: The ruling temporarily preserves Maryland’s existing congressional map and prevents Democrats from using the proposed amendment to target the state’s lone Republican House district.

A cyclosporiasis outbreak tied to contaminated iceberg lettuce imported from Mexico and supplied to Taco Bell has sickened over 11,000 people across 20 different U.S. states.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED: An outbreak of the cyclospora “explosive diarrhea” parasite, which has been linked to imported lettuce from Mexico, has spread to three more U.S. states.
📺 DETAIL:The parasite has sickened 11,458 people across a total of 20 U.S. states so far. Two people have died from the parasite, and hundreds have been hospitalized, according to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The two deaths were reported in Michigan, which is among the most affected states. Both of the deceased had underlying health conditions. Lettuce supplied by Taylor Farms de Mexico has been identified as the source of the outbreak. Specifically, the lettuce was imported from Mexico and supplied to Taco Bell restaurants.First identified in July, the parasite has now spread to Georgia, Tennessee, and Texas.The announcement of the most recent states to be affected by the outbreak came on Thursday. The parasite causes cyclosporiasis, which produces symptoms such as “watery diarrhea,fatigue, and loss of appetite,” according to the Centers for Disease Prevention and Control (CDC). Cyclosporiasis symptoms also include “bloating,cramping, and weight loss,” according to the Centers. “Without treatment, symptoms can last anywhere from a few days to a monthor longer,” wrote the CDC on its website. Public health officials have urged consumers to wash fresh produce thoroughly and cook it when possible, as heat can kill the parasite.
🎯 IMPACT: The outbreak is among the largest foodborne outbreaksin recent U.S. history. As a result of the outbreak, sales of leafy greens, such as lettuce, have fallen by as much as 30 percent. Vegetable sales also took a hit, declining roughly 16 to 17 percent.Fruit sales have also reportedly declined since the start of the outbreak.
📺 FLASHBACK: The two deaths from the outbreak were reported back in early August. At the time, 193 hospitalizationshad been recorded in the state. Michigan typically has around 50 cases over the course of the year.

President Donald J. Trump has signed an executive order formally establishing the United States Space Academy, a federally chartered institution to provide formal education and training to astronauts and related personnel.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED:President Donald J. Trump has signed an executive order establishing a NASA-led Presidential Commission to develop a federally chartered United States Space Academy.
📺 DETAIL:Announced during a speech on Friday at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston, Texas, the proposed U.S. Space Academy will be modeled on institutions such as West Pointand the U.S. Air Force Academy.The President declared that the U.S. must prepare “an entire generation of skilled service members, engineers, and civil operators.” The Space Academy will be used to train future leaders in space exploration, defense, and technological advancement. The proposed institution will aim to combine technical education with leadership and public service training. Unlike NASA’s Space Camp, the Space Academy will provide formal education and professional developmentto astronauts, scientists, and engineers, along with military personnel and government officials. The Commission will be chaired by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. The Commission has 120 days to produce recommendations, including governance policies, a training curriculum, service obligations, and a permanent location, among other things. At present, Houston, Texas, Colorado Springs, Colorado, Cape Canaveral, Florida, and Huntsville, Alabama, have been floated as potential sites for the Space Academy. The President’s executive orderwas signed soon after his speech on Friday.
💬 KEY QUOTE: “I said I’ll do it, but it’s got to be top line, it’s got to be the equivalent of the others,” said President Trump, emphasizing that the Space Academy’s standards would be made to match West Point and the U.S. Air Force Academy.
🎯 IMPACT: This represents the first major steptowards establishing a U.S. Space Academy. This policy represents a continuation of space-related policies implemented during President Trump’s first term, such as spearheading the creation of the U.S. Space Forceand establishing the Artemis program to return American astronauts to the Moon.

Vincente Cortes Quiroz, 37, will also serve three years of supervised release following his prison term, according to federal prosecutors.

The case follows another federal prosecution involving a DACA recipient, Rodolfo Benitez-Garza, who was sentenced in Texas in 2025 to 18 months in prison for participating in a straw-purchasing scheme involving firearms intended for Mexico.
🎯 IMPACT: The case is likely to fuel renewed scrutiny of DACA and immigration enforcement, particularly over whether recipients who commit serious federal crimes should continue receiving protection from deportation. It also highlights concerns about illegal firearms trafficking and the ability of federal authorities to prevent prohibited or fraudulent purchases from licensed gun dealers.

I look forward to working with Ghent University rector Petra De Sutter to continue the relationship between the university and the United States. I am grateful for her willingness to listen to voices calling for protecting academic freedom.” — U.S. Ambassador Bill White on X.

sources.news_title: U.S. enters into oil agreement with Venezuela, Trump says
US-Venezuela Oil Pact Links 65bn Barrels to $100bn Investment Push
sources.text:
A sweeping US-Venezuela oil pact links American access to projects containing more than 65 billion barrels of proven reserves with a push to attract about $100 billion of private investment, offering Washington a long-term Western Hemisphere energy hedge while giving Caracas a potential route to rebuild its weakened oil industry.
The bilateral framework covers 17 strategic oilfields and targets production of more than 1.5 million barrels per day, according to interim President Delcy Rodríguez, who says the agreement will run for 25 years. US officials have separately said the private venture involved has been granted 100-year development rights over the fields. Full contracts have not been published, leaving the relationship between the two periods unclear.
The scale is considerable. Venezuela holds roughly 303 billion barrels of proven reserves — the world’s largest national total — but produces only about 1.25 million bpd after years of underinvestment, mismanagement and sanctions. The 65 billion barrels covered by the agreement represent more than one-fifth of that reserve base.
President Donald Trump has described the arrangement as giving the US majority control over the reserves. More precisely, however, Venezuela retains sovereign ownership of its hydrocarbons while US interests are expected to gain substantial economic rights through the new operating structure, including equity and access to crude production.
US Gains a Western Hemisphere Energy Hedge
For Washington, the strategic prize is preferential access to a vast oil resource close to US refineries, rather than ownership of the oil underground.
A US official says the arrangement gives Washington 55% of the venture’s effective output through a combination of ownership and rights to purchase crude at cost. Some of that oil could be directed toward rebuilding the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve and supplying military requirements.
Additional Venezuelan production could also provide Gulf Coast refiners with more heavy crude and strengthen Western Hemisphere supply at a time when the Iran war has exposed the vulnerability of Middle Eastern energy routes.
The benefits, however, are unlikely to arrive quickly. Reserves are not production. Venezuela’s ageing fields, power network and export infrastructure require substantial rehabilitation, while much of its heavy and extra-heavy crude is more expensive and technically demanding to develop and process than conventional oil.
Chevron, already operating in Venezuela, is among the companies expected to finalise talks under the country’s new energy framework. Its existing infrastructure and operating experience could make it an important bridge between political agreements and additional barrels.
Trump’s claim that the agreement will lower US gasoline prices should therefore be treated as a longer-term ambition. Pump prices depend on global crude markets, refinery margins and domestic supply conditions, while materially increasing Venezuelan production could take years.
Venezuela Trades Access for Capital
For Caracas, the economic bargain is greater foreign participation in exchange for capital, technology, operational expertise and access to international markets.
Rodríguez says the programme could eventually generate about $209 billion in revenue for the Venezuelan state, based on an assumed oil price of $65 a barrel. She says roughly $19 from each barrel produced and sold under the arrangement would flow to Venezuela.
Higher output could increase dollar earnings, government revenues and import capacity while creating jobs and rehabilitating the country’s most important export industry.
The trade-off is greater long-term foreign involvement in a sector historically regarded as a strategic national asset. That raises questions over contract durability, political opposition and whether future Venezuelan governments would maintain the arrangements.
The decisive question is whether political access to the reserves can attract enough private capital to develop them.
The proposed $100 billion should currently be treated as an investment target, not committed capital expenditure. A complete roster of investors and lenders, project-level commitments and the final mix of equity, debt and government-backed financing has not been disclosed.
For oil companies, the headline reserve figure alone will not determine investment. Returns will depend on development costs, royalties and taxes, sanctions policy, contract enforcement, infrastructure reliability and the ability to repatriate profits.
The strategic exchange is nevertheless clear: Washington is seeking privileged access to one of the world’s largest concentrations of oil, while Caracas is offering greater foreign participation to secure the capital and technology needed to restore production. Whether the pact becomes an energy-market game changer will depend less on the headline 65 billion barrels than on how much of the proposed $100 billion is actually committed — and how quickly investment can turn reserves into commercially viable production.

sources.news_title: Trump 'bangga' bolot minyak Venezuela
sources.text:
WASHINGTON: Amerika Syarikat (AS) bakal memperoleh kawalan majoriti ke atas lebih 65 bilion tong rizab minyak terbukti Venezuela menerusi perjanjian baharu yang diumumkan Presiden Donald Trump.
Trump menyifatkan perjanjian dengan Presiden sementara Venezuela, Delcy Rodriguez, sebagai ‘yang terbesar dalam sejarah dunia’, manakala Setiausaha Negara AS, Marco Rubio, berkata ia akan membawa hampir AS$100 bilion (RM402 bilion) pelaburan swasta ke Caracas.
Presiden AS itu mengumumkan perjanjian tersebut kelmarin menerusi platform media sosialnya, namun butiran mengenai terma perjanjian masih belum didedahkan.
Beliau mendakwa, pentadbirannya berjaya mendapatkan kawalan majoriti ke atas lebih 65 bilion tong rizab minyak terbukti Venezuela tanpa melibatkan kos kepada pembayar cukai Amerika.
Trump berkata, Rubio dan Setiausaha Pertahanan AS, Pete Hegseth, mencapai perjanjian tersebut dengan Rodriguez melalui kerjasama dengan sektor perniagaan swasta.
Menurutnya, perjanjian itu akan meningkatkan lebih dua kali ganda rizab minyak AS.
Beliau juga berkata, perjanjian itu akan membantu menurunkan harga petrol untuk rakyat Amerika ketika beliau berdepan tekanan susulan kejatuhan sokongan menjelang pilihan raya pertengahan penggal pada November.
Venezuela dianggarkan mempunyai 303 bilion tong rizab minyak terbukti, yang merupakan terbesar di dunia.
Kerajaan Venezuela berada di bawah tekanan serta pemantauan ketat pentadbiran Trump sejak AS menggulingkan dan menangkap bekas pemimpin negara itu, Nicolas Maduro, pada Januari lalu.
Washington kemudian membenarkan bekas naib presiden Maduro, Rodriguez, kekal sebagai pemangku presiden dengan syarat beliau ‘tunduk’ kepada pendirian AS.
Trump sebelum ini tidak menyembunyikan hasratnya untuk mendapatkan bekalan minyak Venezuela bagi kepentingan AS.- AGENSI

sources.news_title: Trump announces massive oil deal for US control of Venezuelan reserves
sources.text:
Trump announces massive oil deal for US control of Venezuelan reserves
Photo: The White House / flickr (PDM 1.0)
President Donald Trump announced an oil deal with Venezuela that he called the “biggest oil deal in world history,” claiming it gives the United States majority control over 65 billion barrels of the South American nation’s proven oil reserves.
Trump made the announcement in a post on Truth Social, saying the “historic transaction more than doubles American oil reserves” and “will substantially lower gas prices for all Americans.” The deal followed weeks of negotiations and would give American companies long-term access to a group of Venezuelan oilfields while guaranteeing crude supply to US refineries.
For drivers in Northeast Philadelphia and across the country, the administration is pitching the agreement as a path to cheaper fuel. But significant questions remain about how the deal would work, and whether it can survive legal challenges in Venezuela.
Rubio touts jobs and investment for Venezuela
Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the agreement as a win for both countries. Writing on X, Rubio said it would secure stable, low-cost oil for the US and help lower gas prices.
For Venezuela, Rubio said the deal would bring nearly $100 billion in private investment, support thousands of high-paying jobs and help rebuild the country’s economy. Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodriguez welcomed the agreement, which is expected to bring about $209 billion to the state’s treasury, Al Jazeera reported.
Trump said Secretary of War Pete Hegseth also worked on the deal alongside Rubio, and that it was secured through a partnership with private business “at no cost to the American Taxpayer.”
Venezuela’s oil wealth and years of decline
Venezuela holds the world’s largest proven oil reserves but produces only 1.25 million barrels per day, far below its potential after years of underinvestment, mismanagement and sanctions. The deal represents a dramatic expansion of Washington’s role in the country’s oil industry as the Trump administration seeks to revive production and lock in more crude for US refineries.
Venezuelan officials are preparing to sign agreements next week granting new oil exploration and production rights to companies, particularly US firms. Sources previously told Reuters that a lease model was under consideration, with fields potentially auctioned to US producers.
Key details still undisclosed
Trump did not disclose the structure of the agreement, the fields or companies involved, nor how the US would exercise majority control over the reserves. The arrangement could also face legal and constitutional challenges in Venezuela, where the state retains control over core oil industry activities.
Critics have called the deal predatory. Formal signing of the agreements is expected next week.
